clue.text: Discourse at entering exchange

indicators.note: entering means the little word at goes inside the word for exchange

parts.note: conversion is an exchange, as of currency

explanation.surface: Talk among people gathered at some trading exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' is the conversion of one currency to another, not a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a spoken exchange of ideas, a talk between people.

clue.text: Study a safety-device baffle

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a fuse is a safety device that breaks an electrical circuit

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine a safety device that has someone stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle someone is to bewilder or perplex them.

clue.text: It's very pleasant on the Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone praising the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable or enjoyable is the everyday sense; the French resort city on the Côte d'Azur is the second.

clue.text: Mere lad going wrong, being green

indicators.note: going wrong says the letters of mere lad are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lad going off the rails because he is naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a description of the inexperienced lad, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright gemstone colour, a shade of green.

clue.text: Rising anger in Parisian coppers is no laughing matter

indicators.note: in places the turned anger word inside the coins

parts.note: sous were old French copper coins

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for anger is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Angry French police are not something to joke about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns IRE into ERI, which goes 'in' SOUS. 'coppers' suggests police but means coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grave or weighty is no laughing matter.

clue.text: Small daughter kept in over some trouble

indicators.note: kept in means the daughter's letter is held inside the word for over

parts.note: too means over, excessively, as in overly
D is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: A little girl given detention, leading to a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, a bit of bother.

clue.text: No longer prompt without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for prompt goes round the point

parts.note: prompt means on time, punctual
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Someone who is no longer punctual and has lost focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Former or erstwhile describes something that no longer holds.

clue.text: Fighting craft, as a sharp man said deviously

indicators.note: deviously signals the letters of a sharp man said are rearranged by devious means

explanation.surface: A clever man's remark about warships, said in a crafty way.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1588 Spanish fleet sent against England was a host of warships.

clue.text: Still seen together

explanation.surface: Two words for simultaneous.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Still' can mean nevertheless, and 'together' means simultaneously; both senses fit the phrase.

clue.text: Little page with an affliction but such style!

parts.note: P is the short form of page
an ache is a pain or affliction

explanation.surface: A small pageboy who suffers but carries it off with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence, dash or flair.

clue.text: Most colourful English churchman taken in by others

indicators.note: taken in by means the churchman and English letters go inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree

explanation.surface: A clergyman taken in by the rest is the most flamboyant.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by clergy, so it stands for a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: The most vividly red is the most colourful in a literal sense.

clue.text: Name for a religious lady retaining nothing

indicators.note: retaining means the religious lady holds the zero inside her

parts.note: a nun is a religious woman
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Naming a nun who keeps nothing for herself.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical word for a person, place or thing is a naming word.

clue.text: Stick to sitting in the bar

indicators.note: sitting in means the word to goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: to ban is to bar

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay seated in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but means prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick, as used by a conductor or relay runner.

clue.text: Dunderhead and his badly-cooked food

parts.note: the head of Dunder, its first letter, is D

indicators.note: badly cooked means the letters of his are messed up

explanation.surface: An idiot and his poorly prepared meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Dunderhead' as 'Dunder head': the head of Dunder, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food served at a meal.

clue.text: Kind instruction

explanation.surface: Two one-word senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or class of thing, as in a religious brotherhood, and a command or directive.

clue.text: Dickens' character making the cigarette popular

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure who makes smoking trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: The receiver of stolen goods who runs a gang of boy pickpockets in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: A body of troops engaged in drop getting cut off

indicators.note: engaged in means the troops are set inside the word for drop

parts.note: to shed is to drop or cast off
RE, the Royal Engineers, a body of British Army troops

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers caught in a parachute drop gets isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army; 'drop' is a verb, to shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn or clipped away with shears means removed by cutting.

clue.text: Swell accommodation!

parts.note: not grand lodgings: the ability to adjust to, or accommodate, the swell of the waves aboard a ship

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a great place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to keep balance on a rolling deck is accommodating oneself to the swell.

clue.text: Old cat — nine possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of cat and nine may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An old cat that might be on its ninth life.
explanation.definitionFit: Very old, belonging to times long past.

clue.text: Room cleaner receiving an order

indicators.note: receiving means the cleaner holds the order inside

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady in British usage
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady being honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning woman; the MBE is a British honour, a member of an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a private or formal one.

clue.text: Trusted leader with cause for duplicity

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of trusted

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: A trusted leader with grounds for double-dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country is the gravest kind of double-dealing.

clue.text: All the same, this suits a lot of people

definitions.text: this suits a lot of people

explanation.surface: A remark on conformity and clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical throughout is one sense; the second is the outfit worn by a whole group of workers or soldiers.

clue.text: Stretches out in a continental luxury car

parts.note: un is French for a
a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Someone lounging in a foreign limousine.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something flat by opening its rolled-up length is to stretch it out.

clue.text: Somehow draws on ahead

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters of draws on are arranged in some way

explanation.surface: Something drawing on into the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Onwards means forward, further ahead.

clue.text: Aim low

explanation.surface: An instruction to aim downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is the first sense; base or ignoble is the second.

clue.text: Is tolerant of speculators

explanation.surface: Someone who puts up with traders.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or put up with, and stock-market dealers who sell in expectation of falling prices.

clue.text: Strike for the return of some marbles

indicators.note: return of means the word for marbles is read backwards

parts.note: taws are marbles, the large ones used for shooting

explanation.surface: Industrial action to get some marbles back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action but is the verb, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit sharply, as at a fly.

clue.text: No American exhibits good sense!

explanation.surface: A remark that Americans lack common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang for practical intelligence or common sense.

clue.text: Superseded top man in a most sardonic mood

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the words most sardonic

explanation.surface: A deposed leader in a bitter mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor, a ruler long since replaced.

clue.text: To honour debts is questionable

parts.note: to dub is to honour with a knighthood
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.surface: Doubt about whether paying what you owe is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful or suspect, open to question.

clue.text: Desire spirit to be shown for a period of five years

parts.note: lust is strong desire
rum is a spirit, a distilled drink

explanation.surface: Craving drink for half a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum was the Roman five-year span between censuses.

clue.text: Gives members salutes

parts.note: presents means gives
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Someone handing out greetings to club members.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a rifle upright before the body is a military salute.
